algorithm.name: Location-concentration ranking from meaningful-work event stream
algorithm.summary: Activity bands rank the N most actively CONCENTRATED canonical locations, not the N most recent events. The event log is the input signal; the output is a ranked list of locations by accumulated work concentration.
steps: 1. Maintain an append-only log of meaningful-work events (ACT-NNN). Each event names the canonical records and/or branches it affects.
2. To compute band assignments, scan the event log within a defined horizon (default: all events, or last H events if the log grows very large).
3. For each canonical record, count how many distinct meaningful-work events within the horizon affected it. This is its ACTIVITY WEIGHT.
4. Rank all canonical records by activity weight descending. Ties broken by most-recent-event timestamp.
5. Top N records by weight = HOT. Next N = WARM. Next N = COOL. Remainder = COLD.
6. Branch-level hottest_activity = the highest band of any member record in that branch.
7. HOT-FILES index is regenerated from the band assignments.
properties: Repeated meaningful work on ONE location increases its weight, concentrating activity there rather than consuming multiple band slots.
One event affecting multiple records increases weight for ALL of them.
A dormant/COLD location receiving new meaningful work immediately gains weight and can jump to HOT if it enters the top N.
A location with a single recent event but no concentration may be outranked by a location with sustained older work. This is intentional: concentration matters more than mere recency.
Clerical/housekeeping events are never logged, so they contribute zero weight.
The algorithm is deterministic: same event log + same N = same band assignments.
Cheap to compute: scan events, count per-record, sort, slice into N-sized bands.
algorithm.configurable_H: null (use all events). May be set to e.g. 50 if the event log grows very large, to bound computation. A horizon of null means all historical work contributes, with natural dilution as more locations accumulate events.
algorithm.recomputation_trigger: Whenever a new ACT-NNN event is appended.

design_principles.1_activity_means_meaningful_work: Activity tracks WHERE Chris/Andi attention and meaningful work is concentrated. NOT document age, timestamps, authority, retrieval preference, or historical importance.
design_principles.2_authority_is_independent: An authoritative record may be COLD. A provisional record may be HOT. Activity NEVER overrides authority.
design_principles.3_retrieval_depth_is_independent: A large historical record is not COLD merely because it is normally retrieved on demand. If meaningful work involves it, its weight increases.
design_principles.4_clerical_does_not_heat: Housekeeping, timestamps, formatting, metadata maintenance, archive manufacture, file moves, automated sync do NOT constitute meaningful activity and are NEVER logged as events.
design_principles.5_reactivation_is_immediate: A COLD location receiving meaningful new work gains weight immediately. No cooling penalty or dormancy delay.
design_principles.6_one_authoritative_state: This file is the SINGLE authoritative activity state. HOT-FILES, SYSTEM-MAP branch annotations, MACHINE-TREE activity bands and RETRIEVAL-INDEX activity bands are ALL derived from this file.
design_principles.7_continuous_evolution: Append new events as work occurs. Recompute bands. Regenerate derived views. No periodic full-corpus reconstruction needed.
design_principles.8_concentration_not_recency: Bands represent concentration of meaningful work at locations, not merely which events happened most recently. Sustained work on one location keeps it hot even if other locations receive a single newer event.

DOES_count: Meaningful test executed or result obtained
New evidence added or significant evidence retrieved for active work
Material edit to a canonical record's operative content
Genuine reactivation of a dormant branch for real work
Significant new dependency or relationship established
Resolution of an uncertainty or conflict
does_NOT_count: Reading a record without changing or actively working with it
A record being referenced by another record unless that reference represents active work

forward_maintenance.adding_work: 1. Append ACT-NNN to event_log. 2. Recount weights for affected records. 3. Re-rank and re-slice into N-sized bands. 4. Regenerate HOT-FILES, update branch_hottest in SYSTEM-MAP, update derived activity in MACHINE-TREE/RETRIEVAL-INDEX.
forward_maintenance.reactivating_cold: Same as adding work. The cold record gains weight from the new event and enters the ranking. If it reaches top N, it becomes HOT immediately.
forward_maintenance.new_project_or_record: Create canonical record with stable ID. First meaningful work event names it. It enters the ranking at weight=1 and may immediately be HOT if the top-N threshold permits.
forward_maintenance.record_supersession: Superseded record stops receiving new events. Its weight naturally decays relative to records still receiving work. It falls through bands as newer locations accumulate more weight.
forward_maintenance.horizon_management: If the event log grows very large, set H to scan only the last H events for weight computation. Older events are preserved as history but stop contributing to band ranking. H=null (all events) is the default.
forward_maintenance.no_reconstruction: Band computation requires only: scan events, count per-record, sort, slice. No full-corpus traversal.
